lines.text: Can you count to a billion? Out loud, every single number.
lines.phonemes: kæn juː kˈaʊnt tʊ ɐ bˈɪliən? ˈaʊt lˈaʊd, ˈɛvɹi sˈɪŋɡəl nˈʌmbɚ.

lines.text: A number a second sounds fair, and even at that pace you'd be counting for about thirty-two years. But the numbers don't stay short.
lines.phonemes: ɐ nˈʌmbɚɹ ɐ sˈɛkənd sˈaʊndz fˈɛɹ, ænd ˈiːvən æt ðæt pˈeɪs juːd biː kˈaʊntɪŋ fɔːɹ ɐbˌaʊt θˈɜːɾitˈuː jˈɪɹz. bˌʌt ðə nˈʌmbɚz dˈoʊnt stˈeɪ ʃˈɔːɹt.

lines.text: Up in the hundreds of millions, every number is a sentence of its own, and you have to say all of it.
lines.phonemes: ˌʌp ɪnðə hˈʌndɹɪdz ʌv mˈɪliənz, ˈɛvɹi nˈʌmbɚɹ ɪz ɐ sˈɛntəns ʌv ɪts ˈoʊn, ænd juː hæv tə sˈeɪ ˈɔːl ʌv ɪt.

lines.text: We know how fast a person really counts, because a man did it, live on the internet, through most of his waking hours, all the way to a million. It took him most of a summer.
lines.phonemes: wiː nˈoʊ hˌaʊ fˈæst ɐ pˈɜːsən ɹˈiəli kˈaʊnts, bɪkˈʌz ɐ mˈæn dˈɪd ɪt, lˈaɪv ɔnðɪ ˈɪntɚnˌɛt, θɹuː mˈoʊst əv hɪz wˈeɪkɪŋ ˈaʊɚz, ˈɔːl ðə wˈeɪ tʊ ɐ mˈɪliən. ɪt tˈʊk hˌɪm mˈoʊst əv ɐ sˈʌmɚ.

lines.text: Keep going at his pace, sleeping when he slept, and the whole count takes nearly four hundred years. That's about five whole lifetimes of nothing but numbers.
lines.phonemes: kˈiːp ɡˌoʊɪŋ æt hɪz pˈeɪs, slˈiːpɪŋ wɛn hiː slˈɛpt, ænd ðə hˈoʊl kˈaʊnt tˈeɪks nˌɪɹli fˈɔːɹ hˈʌndɹɪd jˈɪɹz. ðæts ɐbˌaʊt fˈaɪv hˈoʊl lˈaɪftaɪmz ʌv nˈʌθɪŋ bˌʌt nˈʌmbɚz.

lines.text: Never sleep, or talk twice as fast, and you'd still need centuries.
lines.phonemes: nˈɛvɚ slˈiːp, ɔːɹ tˈɔːk twˈaɪs æz fˈæst, ænd juːd stˈɪl nˈiːd sˈɛntʃɚɹiz.

lines.text: So the word is easy to say once, and the number is out of reach one by one.
lines.phonemes: sˌoʊ ðə wˈɜːd ɪz ˈiːzi tə sˈeɪ wˈʌns, ænd ðə nˈʌmbɚɹ ɪz ˌaʊɾəv ɹˈiːtʃ wˈʌn baɪ wˌʌn.

lines.text: Next envelope: if everyone jumped at once, would the Earth move?
lines.phonemes: nˈɛkst ˈɑːnvəlˌoʊp: ɪf ˈɛvɹɪwˌʌn dʒˈʌmpt ɐtwˈʌns, wʊd ðɪ ˈɜːθ mˈuːv?
